articles.title_orig: ‘GTA 6’ Is Already One Of The Best-Selling Games Ever, Report Says
articles.title_zh: ‘GTA 6’ Is Already One Of The Best-Selling Games Ever, Report Says
articles.content_orig:
It is technically perfect in its rendition of imperfection, evocative in a way that can’t be explained and must be experienced. And it can be experienced on many different levels.
It is technically perfect in its rendition of imperfection, evocative in a way that can’t be explained and must be experienced. And it can be experienced on many different levels.
Grand Theft Auto VI , the sprawling new video game released last week by Rockstar Games , is the latest edition of the most lucrative media franchise on Earth. How lucrative? It made an estimated $3.8 billion on its first day . That’s bigger than the Avengers. It’s bigger than Harry Potter and the Transphobic Author . It’s bigger than the Super Bowl. It’s the biggest single thing in culture right now. And that appears to be confusing a lot of people who don’t play video games. For the uninitiated, GTA is essentially a sandbox crime simulator. It allows you to steal cars, sell drugs, and run over pedestrians as you flee from the cops you haven’t yet shot. It allows you to stick up a Waffle House, drag an ATM through the streets until it breaks open, and murder every civilian in an only lightly fictionalized rendition of the state of Florida.
The fact that this is the most popular thing on the planet seems to be scrambling many brains. I keep seeing the same question from non-gamers: Why ? Why has this video game broken containment and landed in the center of American and even global public discourse? Why does it make so much money? Why is it everywhere ?
I feel like I am well situated to answer these questions, because, while I’m a normal American dad with a wife and children and a full-time job and all the other indicia of normal adult responsibility, I’m also an avid gamer. Most people who play video games will buy only one or two a year ; I probably buy a new game (often on sale) every six to eight weeks. I generally find at least 10 hours a week to play them—though really, the weeks when I only play 10 hours are, like, “election week” or “a week when a hurricane knocked out my power for days.”
So, with my bona fides out of the way: the first thing I tell non-gamers about GTA , or any video game, is that “it’s art.” Thinking about GTA as art helps to explain everything else that’s happening around it, because GTA is the Mona Lisa of this art form. It is technically perfect in its rendition of imperfection. It is evocative in a way that can’t be explained and must be experienced. And it can be experienced on many different levels. Some people want to see the Mona Lisa just to say that they’ve seen it. Some people will see it and not get what all the fuss is about (the French call those people “Americans”). Some people will see it and feel moved to their core. The same thing happens with GTA : It has a fairly linear “Bonnie and Clyde” type of story with a couple of different endings, but no two people will experience GTA in exactly the same way.
Of course, the Mona Lisa isn’t going to pull out a gun and start shooting paintballs at the other portraits. Nor is she going to remove her top and start shaking her money-maker. So let’s get into that. Yes, GTA is violent and hypersexualized. There is a lot of shooting, there are a lot of boobs and penises, and all the violence and sex is delivered with a steady stream of foul language and crude humor. If you want to be mad at the game, the game will give you something to be mad about, no matter your politics. Indeed, right now the people who are most mad at the game are the white-wing manosphere. The game tracks the relationship between the two main characters (who are in a cis-heteronormative relationship) and essentially encourages you to be a “good boyfriend/girlfriend.” The notion of being nice to a woman has made the manosphere lose its mind. Oh no, the game gives you the option to buy flowers for your girlfriend as part of a quest! Men are doomed! You can also not buy her flowers, or you can, I assume, murder the flower-shop guy and take the flowers (but I didn’t try to do that because I am a normal freaking person whose masculinity is not threatened by showing affection).
Just like the sex—or, in the case of the manosphere, the “acknowledging that a woman is a human being”— the violence in GTA is going to turn a lot of people off. But here’s the thing I think most non-gamers do not understand: GTA isn’t the most violent video game on the market. It’s not in the top 10 violent video games that are broadly popular right now. I wouldn’t even rank GTA VI as the most violent video game I’ve played this year . It’s also not the most sexually explicit game I’ve played recently: Baldur’s Gate 3 (a role-playing game that won Game of the Year in 2023) allows you to play with your characters fully nude, if you want to. It famously lets you have sex with a bear.
GTA is not popular because of the violence or sex. The thing that makes GTA popular is the agency you have over the violence. Yes, you can run over pedestrians, but you can also not do that. You can shoot all the cops in the head as you blast your way out of a bank with cash stuffed in the duffel bag, or you can carefully plan your heist so that you trip no alarms and get away without firing a shot. You can’t play the game as a pacifist (you are a criminal; you will be committing crimes; the authorities will try to stop you from committing crimes; this will often lead to violence), but your ultimate body count is your own and reflects your choices, not the game’s.
It’s that agency that makes GTA a totally different experience from other games that are facially far more violent and bloody. If you put me in an average mission in the popular first-person shooter Call of Duty , I’m going to kill a lot of people. The game will call those people “terrorists” because I’m not supposed to feel bad about killing them, but it will give me no success condition other than murdering every terrorist in the compound. In GTA , by comparison, there was an early mission where my friend was kidnapped by odious redneck pig farmers. They were coded as rednecks so that a certain type of person (namely me) wouldn’t feel bad should violence become necessary. Once I freed him, the game gave me the option of
I went with option 3. GTA is popular not because option 3 exists—option 3 exists in pretty much every video game. GTA is popular because options 1 and 2 also exist , so when you choose option 3 you feel it . It makes the killing more of a personal choice than a gameplay mechanic. Most games allow you to kill; GTA is a success because you don’t have to.
Choice and consequence over murder or mercy is not unique to GTA . In fact, I’ve played a lot of games with far more difficult and engaging murder choices than “kill rednecks, yes/no?” But what makes GTA truly special, and a cultural phenomenon rather than simply a very good video game, is that it is a satirical take on us: America in the 2020s. The game is not set in medieval Europe. There are no dragons or witches. It is set in only lightly fictionalized Florida. If you walk down the street in the GTA ’s main city (called “Vice City”), you will feel like you’re walking around Miami.
The game cost well over a billion dollars and 13 years to make, and part of that budget went toward sending game developers to Miami and around Florida to just watch, observe, and report back. It’s reactive in a way never before seen: Random characters will be having random conversations that don’t involve you, and react as one might expect them to if you pull a gun on them: most will run; some will fight; some will just shrug and be like “joke’s on you, I’m broke.”
You will see every body type, fashion choice, race, color, or creed in the game that you might see on any street in America. You’ll hear music blaring out of certain stores. You’ll see car accidents that don’t involve the player at all. One random character tried to steal my car (it didn’t work out well for him).

In an address to slighted Xbox customers, Playtonic explains why a new "Yooka-Laylee" edition is not coming to Xbox Series X |S.
Banjo-Kazooie is one of Xbox's most-requested, and most-dormant franchises, with fans of a certain age awash with nostalgia for early 00s 3D platformers. The genre hasn't exactly remained popular in recent years, but PlayStation's Astrobot has more than proven that there's still juice to be squeezed if the game is positioned properly.
Playtonic took up the Banjo mantle with its spiritual successor, Yooka-Laylee, featuring a superficially similar duo inspired by Rare's golden era.
Given Microsoft's ownership of the Banjo IP, you might expect Yooka-Laylee to have a decent chunk of fans and players on Xbox, but Playtonic says that they're not enough to justify this latest port.
Hi everyone, please read the following regarding the situation for Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition on Xbox Series S/X - https://t.co/IQeesCczo6 November 27, 2026
In a statement on social media, Playtonic says "Bringing Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition to PlayStation 5 and Nintendo Switch 2 has been an exciting adventure," describing the new version complete with visual upgrades and other new content. "Unfortunately, we've had to prioritise our efforts given the technical challenges and costs presented in the creation of this updated version of the game and as a result, we are unable to commit to any additional platforms for the foreseeable future," indirectly referring to Xbox, which isn't getting this new edition.
"We understand the frustration felt by those of you who won't be able to access the Definitive Edition at launch, but unfortunately the cost of bringing it to more platforms just isn't viable for us at this time. As a small team, we hope you guys can understand the challenges we face. Please know that this wasn't an easy decision to make, and we apologise to any of you affected by this."
Game journalist Chris Dring chimed in and suggested that developers are findng it "harder to financially justify" launching on Xbox.
Over the last 18 months, a few devs have told that it's proving harder to financially justify launching on Xbox.
However, GTA 6 has done around 10m on Xbox now. That's a lot of people who have turned on the machine! Could be an opportunity. November 27, 2026
It's certainly true that Xbox is the smallest of the big three platforms by userbase, and purchasing habits are likely skewed due to Xbox Game Pass on top. However, many, many indie developers release on Xbox without an Xbox Game Pass deal and find success regardless. Many of these developers consistently launch games into Xbox Play Anywhere to take advantage of the platform beyond Xbox Series X|S consoles too across PC and cloud, with more than half of games launching with Xbox Play Anywhere per monthly average.
Microsoft has historically been very friendly towards indie developers in recent years, paying out literally billions of dollars via the ID@Xbox program . It may have seen some de-emphasis in recent months however, with new Xbox CEO Asha Sharma taking the reins.
Whether or not we'll eventually see Yooka-Laylee on Xbox remains to be seen, but at least for now, users are stuck with the older versions of the game for the foreseeable.

articles.title_zh: Hollow Knight: Silksong - Sea Of Sorrow DLC Finally Has A Release Date
articles.content_orig:
Heya Gang. It’s Cherry Time!
We’ve just announced three exciting new games being developed by a few of our close friends, and, if that wasn’t enough, there’s now an imminent release date for Hollow Knight: Silksong’s first big content update - Sea of Sorrow! Arriving free for all players on December 11!
You can check out the full presentation right here:
In Sea of Sorrow, players will voyage above and beneath Pharloom’s forgotten ocean, across islands, through forts and into deep caverns beneath the waves. We’ve spent the whole year stuffing this adventure full with all the things you’d expect from Hollow Knight: Silksong - crazed characters, high adventure, and epic bosses! It’s also overflowing with more exceptional music by the eternally talented Christopher Larkin! We’re pretty darn excited to get it into all of your hands on December 11, so please look forward to it.
While we’ve been busy on the vast oceans of the Undersea, our friends Rohan, Lukas and Makoto have been hard at work bringing their own worlds to life, each with its own impressive scope and style. We’d happily speak at length about their talents, but why hear more from us when you can hear directly from the creators themselves? Watch the short docos below and let them introduce you to their games, their inspirations, and their beginnings.
As soon as their games are ready, these new titles will be releasing under the brand new Team Cherry Presents label. But what have we busy cherry-folk got to do with these titles, you ask? We’ll we’re glad you did, because Team Cherry had a hand in each game through our fourth and newest member, Huy Le!
Officially Huy acts as the technical director and on-going support for all the Team Cherry Presents games, building robust foundations, bespoke creation tools, puzzle mechanics, and solving countless issues for each developer as they arise. But Huy’s also become something of a secret weapon on the Cherry side, tagging in to assist on Silksong (and now Sea of Sorrow) during the intensive lead-ups to launch. Initially that meant taking on some of Silksong’s many ports, but ultimately it’s included much more - such as resolving countless bugs and implementing integral features (Autosaves, Achievements, HD rumble!).
As a long-time team of three people, adding a fourth member is a big deal! So please everyone welcome Huy to the unit and to Team Cherry Presents.
And finally, a physical news drop! Just last week, our friends at Fangamer unveiled a whole bunch of adorable new Hollow Knight: Silksong merch. They’ve revealed pins, posters, plush and more! A big thank you to them for their continued passion for the world of Hollow Knight, and an extra big thanks for creating the cutest, softest singing-Sherma around.
fangamer.com Worldwide, fangamer.eu UK & EU, fangamer.jp Japan
That’s a wrap on Cherry Time! Watch those stylish docos! Jump over and wishlist the new games on Steam! We’ll be sharing more details about these games soon, and on our own ever-ambitious plans, but for now Sea of Sorrow is imminent and Team Cherry has to start prepping!

articles.title_zh: SpaceX stock rises after Musk pledges annual share giveaway for kids
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Elon Musk says SpaceX could be worth around $128 quintillion, or 75 million times its value today.
It would have to colonize other planets and harness a tiny fraction of the Sun's energy, he said.
"I recommend holding on to your shares," Musk posted on X.
Elon Musk is going galactic with his latest claim of what SpaceX might be worth one day: $128 quintillion.
That's 128 billion billions, or 128 trillion millions, or 128 followed by 18 zeros: 128,000,000,000,000,000,000.
"If SpaceX succeeds in making life multiplanetary and harnessing even a millionth of the Sun's energy, it will be worth about a million times the current global economy," Musk said in an early morning X post on Thursday.
The IMF puts the value of the world economy at around $128 trillion. Musk's post suggests SpaceX could be worth a million times that much, or $128 quintillion. That would be a roughly 75 million-fold increase from its $1.7 trillion market capitalization as of Wednesday's close.
"These are obviously absurdly difficult goals, but there is a path to achieving them," Musk wrote. "I recommend holding on to your shares."
Musk's post implies that a single SpaceX share, worth around $127 at Wednesday's close, could one day be worth $9.5 billion or so, assuming no dilution.
The world's wealthiest man is no stranger to making wild, unfounded claims about SpaceX's potential value. He posted in October that the maker of Starlink, Starship, Grok, and X could eventually be worth " orders of magnitude more than the current Earth economy."
Musk later posted that wasn't a "statement of extreme confidence," but a belief that "there is such a path and the probability of achieving it is not zero."
SpaceX generated $14.6 billion of revenue last quarter , up 161% from the same period last year, and swung from a $1.1 billion net loss to a $4.4 billion net income.
Musk posted in October that SpaceX hitting $1 trillion in annual revenue in 2028 was " no longer impossible ." Even if it reaches that mark, then grows revenue another 1,000-fold to $1 quadrillion, that would still be less than 1% of $128 quintillion.
He made his latest claim about SpaceX's potential price tag after pledging to match the company's gift of one share to every active Trump Account.
The rocket maker said it was part of his commitment to give one of his SpaceX shares to " every kid in America " next year.
If you enjoyed this story, be sure to follow Business Insider on Yahoo.

articles.content_orig:

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman stepped in this summer to persuade the Trump administration to stop pressuring Venezuela over its OPEC membership, two people familiar with the matter have told Reuters.
Saudi Arabia is the group's top producer and its de facto leader.
The intervention came after Washington urged two of OPEC's founding members, Venezuela and Iraq , to consider quitting the organization earlier this year, according to ten people familiar with the matter. The administration also prevented Venezuela from paying its annual membership dues.
These moves, previously unreported, amount to a direct challenge to a body that President Donald Trump has long accused of keeping oil prices artificially high.
At the time, U.S. officials were pressing both countries to raise oil production and investment, and some worried that OPEC's production limits could eventually constrain those ambitions, according to people familiar with the discussions.
In Iraq, Prime Minister Ali Faleh al-Zaidi raised the possibility of leaving OPEC at a government meeting this summer after discussions with US officials who encouraged the idea, two people familiar with the matter said.
Iraq's oil ministry pushed back, persuading al-Zaidi to keep Iraq in the group and instead seek a higher production quota, the people said. The United States holds powerful leverage over both countries.
It controls Venezuela's access to state funds following the January ouster of Nicolas Maduro , while Iraq's oil revenues continue to pass through an account at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, a relic of the 2003 Iraq War .
The State Department did not answer questions about whether it had prevented Venezuela from paying its OPEC membership fee. But it confirmed Washington has the power to decide on Venezuela's use of state funds, now held in a U.S.-controlled account set up after Maduro's removal.
"The Department receives disbursement requests from the interim Venezuelan government and reviews the requests, including against a list of approved and prohibited uses of ​the foreign Government Deposit Funds," a State Department official told Reuters .
The official said lower-level U.S. officials may have raised the question of leaving OPEC with Venezuela's government earlier this year, but that "it has ⁠not been among the issues raised by high-level officials."
The State Department's conversations with Iraq, meanwhile, "have focused on improving energy infrastructure to increase production and transportation of energy, not OPEC," the official said. Representatives for OPEC and for the governments of Venezuela, Iraq, and Saudi Arabia did not respond to requests for comment.
The U.S. maneuvers add strain to an organization that has already lost four members since 2019, and whose share of the global oil market recently hit a low on the back of disruptions caused by the US and Israeli war on Iran , another OPEC founding member.
"The risk of OPEC fracture is rising," said Dan Alamariu, chief geopolitical strategist at Alpine Macro. The United Arab Emirates announced its exit from OPEC earlier this year after growing frustrated with the group's production caps, while Angola , Ecuador and Qatar quit in 2024, 2020 and 2019, respectively.
There are no indications the U.S. was involved in those decisions.
OPEC was founded in Baghdad in September 1960 by oil-producing countries seeking to assert more control over a global market dominated by a handful of Western oil companies.
Founded by Iraq, Iran, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait , and Venezuela, OPEC now has 11 members. It has also formed an alliance with several other producer countries, including Russia , called OPEC+, which regularly meets to set coordinated production levels.
Trump has repeatedly attacked OPEC throughout his decades-long business and political career, calling it a cartel and a monopoly profiting from the rest of the world. Over the past decade, though, the U.S. has become the world's largest oil producer, turning it from an OPEC customer into its main rival for oil market share.
After the U.S. seized Maduro in January, the State Department opened discussions with Venezuelan officials in Washington on whether the country should leave OPEC, five people familiar with the matter told Reuters. They did not identify the individuals who took part in those discussions.
Trump wanted US oil majors to revive Venezuela's oil output, something he said would shore up energy security in the Western Hemisphere, and worried that OPEC policy decisions could hinder that plan, the sources said. In August, Trump said it was up to Venezuela whether to leave OPEC.
U.S. officials also held talks this summer with Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh al-Zaidi, encouraging Iraq's departure from OPEC as US oil majors Exxon Mobil and Chevron planned major new investments there, two people familiar with the matter said.
Al-Zaidi later raised the issue at a government meeting. His oil ministry persuaded him to stay and instead potentially seek a higher OPEC quota, they said. The issue could come up again, as some elements of Iraq's ruling coalition favor leaving OPEC and OPEC+, which they view as dominated by Saudi Arabia and Russia, the people said.
There is no indication Washington has sought to block Baghdad's OPEC dues. After the U.S. invasion of Iraq in 2003, the United States began routing Iraq's oil revenues through an account at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York.
That structure remains in place more than two decades later. This year, the US threatened to starve Iraq of its oil money if it didn't cut Iran's influence in its government.
OPEC membership fee payments are typically due in the first quarter of each year and fund staff salaries, research, and travel at the OPEC Secretariat in Vienna . Unlike the United Nations , where dues are scaled to the size of a country's economy, OPEC splits the fees equally among members at around 2.8 million euros ($3.08 million) each.
The price tag is tiny compared to OPEC oil revenues, but paying it carries symbolic importance as a marker of continued membership in an organization Caracas helped create. Washington argued Venezuela could spend the money on more important matters, one person familiar with the country's relationship with OPEC said.
OPEC has the discretion to disregard unpaid membership fees, and is not planning to expel Venezuela over the issue, two OPEC sources told Reuters. Washington's control of Venezuela's oil revenues and finances has led some in the South American country to refer to their country as a U.S. protectorate, instead of a sovereign nation.
The Government Accountability Office opened a formal investigation in July into the administration's management and disbursement of Venezuelan oil revenues, following congressional requests for transparency.
The Trump administration has said Venezuela's oil revenues are being used to meet the needs of the Venezuelan people, including to pay government salaries and fund essential services. Reuters could not establish when exactly the U.S. rejected the OPEC dues payment request.
Venezuela is currently exempt from OPEC+ oil output quotas as its production has collapsed from historical highs due to years of sanctions and mismanagement. The country pumped about 1.2 million barrels per day in September, according to OPEC figures.
Its state oil company, PDVSA , said it plans to reach 1.5 million bpd by the end of next year. OPEC last regulated Caracas' output with quotas in 2017-2018 when the country's target was around 2 million bpd. The country's return to the quota system is unlikely until it hits that level again, a source familiar with Venezuela's OPEC position said.

articles.title_orig: Google Gemini may expose private emails to reviewers
articles.title_zh: Google Gemini may expose private emails to reviewers
articles.content_orig:
Cybersecurity threats escalate as Leah Siskind analyzes Google’s warning about hackers using AI to automate cyberattacks against companies. Discussing the battle between defenders and attackers with John Roberts, the FDD AI Research fellow references Anthropic’s release of advanced models months ago. Siskin warns that super advanced AI models now have the dangerous ‘ability to detect vulnerabilities’ in software systems.
Think about everything sitting in your Gmail inbox right now. Maybe there's a conversation with your doctor, a recent bank statement or a personal message you never intended anyone else to read. Your Google Drive may hold years of private documents. You probably don't spend much time thinking about who might see that information beyond the people you share it with. But what happens when you connect those services to Google's Gemini AI assistant ?
An independent researcher has raised concerns about how Gemini handles information retrieved from connected Gmail and Google Drive accounts. The findings prompted questions about whether some private content could end up in conversations reviewed by humans.
We contacted Google, and the company confirmed that some information retrieved from connected Gmail and Drive accounts may be seen by human reviewers under certain circumstances. Google stressed that these connections are off by default. Here's what you should know before giving Gemini access to your personal information.
Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.
Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.
Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.
AI CHATBOT PRIVACY: WHAT YOUR AI MAY KNOW ABOUT YOU
Google's Gemini assistant can retrieve information from connected Gmail accounts to answer questions, raising concerns about how private emails may be handled. (Thomas Trutschel/Photothek via Getty Images)
An independent researcher using the name thisisme6598 published findings on GitHub, raising questions about the way Gemini retrieves information from connected Gmail and Google Drive accounts . The researcher tested Gemini using a personal Google Account with connected apps enabled. According to the published findings, Gemini sometimes retrieved information from emails or files during conversations without someone explicitly asking it to search Gmail or Drive. For example, the researcher described asking Gemini whether an internet service bill seemed too expensive. During some tests, Gemini reportedly retrieved billing information from Gmail, including payment amounts, account details and confirmation numbers.
In certain instances, the researcher reported that Gemini returned several sentences directly from an email and, in some tests, the entire email, including its headers. The researcher argues that this behavior creates a privacy concern because information retrieved into a Gemini conversation may become eligible for human review. However, the published findings do not establish that a human reviewer actually accessed the researcher's emails. Google told CyberGuy that the reported retrieval was standard behavior for someone who had voluntarily connected their apps. The company also emphasized that retrieved files remain visible only to the authenticated account holder and are not exposed publicly through this process.
Yes, under certain circumstances. Google's own Connected Apps privacy documentation confirms that trained human reviewers, including service providers, may review a subset of information processed through Gemini's connected apps. That information can include summaries or excerpts from relevant Gmail messages and Google Drive documents.
In some cases, Google acknowledges that reviewers may see a complete email or file if it is short or especially relevant to the request. Google also says human reviewers may access some Gmail inbox content when investigating abuse or harm or responding to submitted feedback.
The company uses these reviews to evaluate Gemini's responses and improve its services.
Simply using Gmail or Google Drive does not subject your private content to this review process. The concern involves information retrieved after someone voluntarily connects those services to consumer Gemini. Google says it does not train generative AI models directly on someone's entire Gmail inbox or Drive. However, relevant information processed during Gemini conversations may be used for model improvement, depending on account settings. Google specifically warns against connecting apps containing confidential information someone would be uncomfortable having a reviewer see.
We contacted Google directly to ask whether human reviewers could access Gmail messages or Drive files processed through the consumer Gemini app. We also asked whether the company had changed its privacy disclosures, notified existing customers and provided ways to prevent human review. A Google spokesperson told CyberGuy:
"Gmail and Google Drive’s core privacy protections remain unchanged, and your private emails and files are not reviewed by humans simply by using Gmail, Drive, or built-in Workspace features. Connecting those apps to the consumer Gemini app is off by default — it’s an optional way to get more personalized, time-saving answers across your Google apps when you want them. Users can disconnect their apps in Gemini settings at any time without losing access to Gemini’s core features."
Google also confirmed that when someone connects their apps to consumer Gemini with activity saving enabled, a small subset of conversations may undergo human review. Those conversations can contain relevant information retrieved from connected services. Before trained service providers review the material, Google says it separates the conversations from the associated Google Account and takes steps to reduce identifying information. The company also disputes the suggestion that the researcher's findings demonstrate public exposure of private files.
Another part of the controversy involves changes to Google's public privacy disclosures . In Oct. 2023, Google published a blog post about its approach to generative AI privacy. The company said that content from Gmail, Docs and Drive accessed through Bard's Workspace extensions would not be seen by human reviewers or used to train the Bard model.
On Oct. 16, 2026, Google added an update to that same blog post. The new language explains that Google has introduced additional optional features allowing people to connect Workspace information to other Google services. Google says that when someone enables these newer features, a subset of the information may be used to train generative AI models, depending on their settings. It may also undergo human review in limited circumstances. The researcher argues that the change represents a reversal of Google's earlier privacy commitment.
However, Google's original statement concerned Bard's Workspace extensions, while the updated disclosure addresses newer connected features. The available evidence does not establish that Google quietly changed the underlying handling of information in existing connections. We asked Google whether people who previously connected their accounts were notified about the updated disclosures or asked to provide additional consent. Google's response did not directly address those questions. Instead, the company emphasized that the newer connections are optional and can be disabled. articles.title_orig: Rare turtles found inside baggage at Amsterdam airport
articles.title_zh: Rare turtles found inside baggage at Amsterdam airport
articles.content_orig:
An official holds one of the seized Vallarta mud turtles - they are now receiving  care at a specialised sanctuary
Twenty-six "very rare" turtles have been seized from a traveller's checked baggage at Amsterdam's Schiphol airport, a Dutch government agency has said.
The Netherlands Food and Consumer Product Safety Authority (NVWA) said a man flying from Mexico to Hong Kong via the airport was arrested on Saturday after the Vallarta mud turtles were found by customs officers.
The endangered species, thought to be the smallest freshwater turtles in the world with a maximum length of about 10cm (4in), were wrapped in duct tape to prevent them from moving.
The NVWA said they were "presumably stolen" from the wild in their native Mexico.
It said most of the turtles were found in a box with a toy car, while the others were in a closed sock inside a suitcase.
The arrested man remains in custody and an investigation is under way.
Meanwhile, the turtles are receiving care at a "specialised sanctuary", the NVWA said.
In 2025, the US NGO Turtle Island estimated that no more than 300 Vallarta mud turtles existed in the wild.
They are listed as critically endangered on a list published by the International Union for Conservation of Nature.
According to environmental news outlet Mongabay, a Vallarta mud turtle can sell for $10,000 (Â£7,500) or more on the black market in Asia.
Other cases of live turtles being smuggled to Hong Kong have been reported this year.
In October, customs authorities in Hong Kong were reported to have seized eight turtles , external that were thought to be endangered. The reptiles had an estimated market value of about $54,000.
Three months prior, Hong Kong customs detected two separate smuggling cases , external . Some 42 live turtles, with a total estimated market value of $210,000 were seized.

articles.title_orig: All safe codes in GTA 6 and where to find them
articles.title_zh: All safe codes in GTA 6 and where to find them
articles.content_orig:
Regardless of whether you're exploring criminal compounds or strange research outposts in GTA 6 , you'll frequently come across locked safes full of cash , valuables and illegal goods to fence off . Annoyingly, the residents of Vice City are damn good at keeping their valuables secure, and these safes are tricky to get into unless you use explosives, which bring unwanted attention.
To counter that, you'll need to find safe codes , which you'll discover by exploring. They're well worth the effort though, as they let you crack open safes without making a sound. Below, we've covered where to find all the safe codes in GTA 6 , so you can bypass every safe door and loot all the valuables inside.
Below, we've listed every safe in GTA 6 and the code required to open it. If you want to know how to find the codes for these safes, we've gone into more detail further down the page. Click each safe you want a more detailed explanation for, and you'll skip right there.
Here's every safe and safe code in GTA 6 :
This page is a work in progress. More safes and solutions coming soon!
The safe is found while completing the Kingpin Bowling alley Illegal Operation in Port Gellhorn. Track down the storage room , and look in the office adjacent to it . You'll find the safe in the back left-hand corner.
Found while completing the Brooks and Boatworks Illegal Operation in Port Gellhorn. You'll find an office on the right-hand side of the compound , near the boat in front of the warehouse. On the wall inside is a map , with multiple safe codes printed on it. The Kingpin Bowling Alley code is included.
The safe is found while completing the Brooks and Boatworks Illegal Operation in Port Gellhorn. It's located in the room up the stairs to your left when entering the front doors of the Brooks and Boatworks warehouse. It's to the left of the pool table, near a white plastic chair.
Found while completing the Brooks and Boatworks Illegal Operation in Port Gellhorn. You'll find an office on the right-hand side of the compound , near the boat in front of the warehouse. On the wall inside is a map , with multiple safe codes printed on it. The Brooks and Boatworks safe code is included.
The safe is found while completing the La Cascara Illegal Operation in Port Gellhorn. It's locked in a small cell in the centre of the motel's top floor .
Found while completing the Brooks and Boatworks Illegal Operation in Port Gellhorn. You'll find an office on the right-hand side of the compound , near the boat in front of the warehouse. On the wall inside is a map , with multiple safe codes printed on it. The La Cascara Motel safe code is included.
Found in the Pelican Valley Outpost in Pelican Valley. Upon entering the house in the centre of the outpost, you'll find the safe directly to your left.
While exploring the house in the centre of the Pelican Valley Outpost, view the engravings in the floor in the bedroom. You'll see that " CLEAVES " is scratched into the floor. Once you've viewed it, head to the computer in the living room and choose CLEAVES when asked for a password. It'll reveal a clue, claiming that the code is " double success ."
After a nasty surprise upon exiting the PC screen, head to the shed near the main house, and you'll find a smashed crab tank inside. Near the tank is a list of crab statistics. One of the crabs in the list is highlighted, with a note claiming 00.36 was a "success" . Double 00.36 and you'll have your code.
Found in the Nova Auto Junkyard as part of an Illegal Operation in Hamlet . Head to the bottom of the junkyard and break into the garage near the broken-down school bus. Inside, you'll spot the safe in a storage room.
In the same garage as the safe, you'll find the '77 Albany Teniente Manana low rider , which counts as valuable. Read the number plate, and you'll get the safe code.
Found in Delights Cabaret in Port Gellhorn. You can't access the safe until you complete the story mission " Afternoon Delight ," at which point you'll be guided to the safe in the back of the club.
As the mission begins, Jason and Lucia will receive a text from Vicki, revealing the safe code.
Found while completing the Farm Fix Meth Lab Illegal Operation in Belville . Enter the main drug lab in Farm Fix, then cross the second-floor catwalk to reach an office. The safe is located inside this office.
The code is found in the back room of Farm Fix's main drug lab. When entering the room, you'll see some glowing cabinets, and to the right of them, a small workbench. You'll find a notepad on top of this workbench with the safe code.
Found while completing the Saber Shipping Facility Illegal Operation in Vice City's Salton district . In the main shipping building, look for an office on the second floor. You'll find the safe in the corner.
The code for the safe is found in the same office as the safe . Look for a map on the wall, directly opposite where you entered the office . On this map, you'll see three codes. Jason or Lucia will automatically memorise the code, but it's the top code labelled on the map.
Found while completing the Casa Guardia Illegal Operation in Vice City's Little Cuba district . Head to the second-floor landing of Casa Guardia , and you'll find the safe behind a desk, above the entrance to the building.
The code for the safe is found while completing the Saber Shipping Facility Illegal Operation in Vice City's Salton district . Head to the second floor of the Shipping Facility and look for an office. Directly opposite where you enter the office, you'll see a map on the wall .
On this map, you'll see three codes. Jason or Lucia will automatically memorise the code, but it's the middle code on the map.
Found while completing the Saber Shipping Yard Illegal Operation in Vice City's Little Cuba district . When raiding the main shipping yard building, look for an office at the back of the building. Beside the desk, you'll find the safe.
The code for the safe is found while completing the Saber Shipping Facility Illegal Operation in Vice City's Salton district . Head to the second floor of the Shipping Facility and look for an office. Directly opposite where you enter the office, you'll see a map on the wall .
On this map, you'll find three codes. Jason or Lucia will automatically memorise the code, but it's the bottom code on the map.
Found while completing the Janjak's Garage Illegal Operation in Vice City's La Perle district. You'll find it in the shop, directly to your left when entering through the front gate. Track down the office area of the shop, and you'll find the safe.
After finding the safe, look in the kitchen to your left. On the fridge, you'll spot a post-it note, which you can read to find the safe code.
Found in the back of Victoria Lee Jeweler in Capri's town centre . When holding up the shop, you can find the safe in the back rooms , next to the store's kitchen counters.
When heading through the staff door on the shop floor, enter the first door on your left. Inside the office it leads to, you'll find a post-it note with the code for the safe beside a laptop.
Found in the back of Richardson Jewelry & Diamonds in Vice City's Downtown district . After entering the back door, you'll find it on your right. The safe is mandatory, as you'll have to open it as part of Yasmani's Jewelry Jobs.
You'll automatically get this safe code as part of the Yasmani's Jewelry Jobs mission chain.
Found in the back of Donovan Banks & Co in Vice City's Peacock Bay district . After entering the back of the store, you'll find it on your left. The safe is mandatory, as you'll have to open it as part of Yasmani's Jewellery Jobs.
You'll automatically get this safe code as part of the Yasmani's Jewelry Jobs mission chain.
And that's that for safe codes. Need more GTA 6 help? Be sure to check out our list of all weapons in GTA 6 , as well as the how to get the fastest car and find a rocket launcher early . If none of those appeal though, you can always find our full list of GT

articles.title_orig: Spain’s election could pull Madrid closer to Trump’s Washington
articles.title_zh: Spain’s election could pull Madrid closer to Trump’s Washington
articles.content_orig:
Spanish voters head to the polls on Sunday for a snap election that could bring down socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, who has repeatedly clashed with U.S. President Donald Trump.
It could also put the far right in government for the first time in the country's modern democratic era.
The center-right Popular Party is the frontrunner, and it could win a majority with far-right Vox, according to El País ' s final polling averages . A government led by the PP could shift Spain's approach to Washington, Beijing and NATO.
It's the first test of whether Europe's mainstream conservatives are willing to bring the far right into government, ahead of elections in France and Poland next year.
Despite Spain's economy growing 2.7% year over year in the third quarter, more than twice the euro zone's 1.3%, the campaign has been dominated by housing and cost-of-living crises.
Inflation soared to 4.9% in the year to October, above a euro zone average of 4%. November's flash estimate published Friday showed Spanish inflation cooling to 4.1%, still well above the 2.3% reading at the start of the year. In an October YouGov survey, 53% of respondents named housing one of the country's two most important issues.
Home purchase prices nearly doubled in the decade to the second quarter of 2026, according to Eurostat . In 2025, house prices rose nearly three times as fast as household incomes, the European Commission said.
Nationwide protests began after an 87-year-old woman died two weeks after being evicted from her Madrid apartment in September.
Sánchez called the snap election after lawmakers rejected two government decrees designed to broaden housing protections, including limiting rent increases and blocking certain evictions and automatic lease renewals. Congress later ratified a revised version of one decree, limiting rent increases and evictions in some circumstances.
Sánchez has made a name for himself internationally after clashing with Trump over NATO spending, the war in Gaza and Spain's refusal to let U.S. forces use its bases for operations against Iran. Trump even threatened to cut off "all trade" with Spain during the dispute over the bases.
At a Nov. 21 rally in Tenerife, Sánchez asked: "What good has President Trump brought to the United States and, by extension, to the world?"
He has also told voters that the PP and Vox would roll back government cost-of-living assistance. Days before the election, Sánchez's government approved 1.21 billion euros ($1.33 billion) to extend public transport discounts through 2027 and approved a general pay increase of up to 4.5% for 2027.
But in a final pre-election survey for El Español on Nov. 23, 66% of respondents gave Sánchez a failing grade and 29.5% a passing one. His government has faced scrutiny over its handling of the Ceuta migrant crisis, two deadly train collisions this year and corruption cases involving people close to the prime minister.
PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo, the current favorite to replace Sánchez, has made alleged government corruption and inflation central to his campaign. At a Nov. 22 rally in Murcia, he said the government wanted voters to forget "that inflation is eating into your pay check, that you can't afford a home, that you're paying more than ever for everything."
The PP led the final El País polling average, published Nov. 24, with 31.4%, followed by Sánchez's Socialists at 29.1% and Vox at 17.9%. Several seat projections put the PP and Vox above the 176 seats needed for a majority in the 350-seat lower house. If Vox joins a government, it would be the first far-right party to do so since Spain returned to democracy after Francisco Franco, the dictator who ruled for 40 years, died in 1975.
The PP wants to repeal the 2023 housing law and scrap rent caps in designated high-pressure areas. It proposes speeding up construction permits and lowering taxes on first homes for buyers under 40. Vox also wants to repeal the housing law and would prioritize Spanish citizens for subsidized housing and public services.
Sánchez's Socialists want to extend renter protections and make at least a quarter of new homes public or permanently price-restricted. It would use proceeds from a bank levy to support housing, which it says will raise a further $1.5 billion. The PP has pledged to scrap this.
The PP also favors easing climate rules, extending the life of nuclear plants and replacing a decree that sets tight new renewable-power requirements on data centers with large new grid connections.
A PP-Vox coalition would have its tensions, with immigration likely to be a major pressure point as Vox has an increasingly hard line on deportation and the militarization of some borders. The parties clashed in regional governments over the distribution of unaccompanied migrant children, leading Vox to quit several coalitions in 2024.
Immigration has since gained more prominence amid the government's handling of reports that more than 70,000 people crossed from Morocco into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta on July 30 and 31.
"Immigration has played a significant role in supporting Spain's recent growth, a strong role for Vox could complicate the government's ability to sustain that," said Jess Middleton, senior Europe analyst at risk intelligence company Verisk Maplecroft.
The parties also differ on defense commitments: both support more investment, but neither has committed to NATO's target of spending 5% of GDP on defense. The PP pledges closer NATO cooperation, while Vox puts greater emphasis on border security.
The PP favors closer integration with the European Union, while Vox wants more independence from it. The success or failure of a PP-Vox partnership will also have wider lessons for Europe "where long-standing firewalls against far-right parties are coming under strain," added Middleton, pointing to the rise of Germany's AfD and the prospect of Marine Le Pen potentially winning next year's election in France.
A shift to the right could improve relations between the U.S. and Spain. Sánchez used his tenure to strengthen ties with Beijing, the country's largest goods trading partner outside the EU.
The U.S. remained Spain's largest source of foreign direct investment. Flows more than doubled to 11.6 billion euros in the 12 months through June 2026, from 5.1 billion euros in the previous 12 months, according to Spain's Economy Ministry.
Carla Hobbs, head of the European Council on Foreign Relations' Madrid office, expects a PP-led government to seek closer ties with Washington and bring its China policy more in line with the EU's. articles.title_orig: A Chinese consumer advocate is stranded in South Korea as a crackdown in China targets campaigners
articles.title_zh: A Chinese consumer advocate is stranded in South Korea as a crackdown in China targets campaigners
articles.content_orig:
FILE - Wang Hai, founder of Beijing Dahai Business Consultancy, checks his smartphone during an interview on June 18, 2015. (AP Photo/Mark Schiefelbein, File)
WASHINGTON (AP) — Chinese consumer rights advocate Wang Hai has spent three decades exposing counterfeit goods and seeking compensation for buyers. In recent months, he left China fearing he was a target of the authorities, but now he is stranded in South Korea with his family, facing possible deportation home.
Wang, a well-known campaigner against counterfeit goods, said China invalidated his passport and South Korean authorities rejected his asylum. The United States also revoked his tourist visa, narrowing his options for leaving South Korea and deepening his fears of being sent back to China.
Chinese authorities launched a campaign against organized crime in July, saying they would target “malicious compensation claims.” Since then, authorities have arrested at least 100 people for allegedly extorting businesses through anti-counterfeiting work or consumer compensation claims, according to official statements reviewed by The Associated Press.
Wang said the arrests made him fear he could be next, prompting him to leave a country where official Chinese media had once praised him for his role as an anti-counterfeiting activist.
China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs told The Associated Press it was not aware of Wang’s case. The Ministry of Public Security did not respond to a request for comment.
The quagmire in which Wang, 53, and his family have found themselves has drawn concerns from rights advocates over China’s efforts to target critics abroad and the narrowing options for people seeking refuge in the U.S.
“The Chinese government’s practice of transnational repression is well documented, including in South Korea,” said Yaqiu Wang, senior China researcher at Human Rights Watch, based in Washington, and “there is no doubt that the Trump administration has created a far more hostile environment for immigrants, and even visitors.”
Wang spoke to the AP from South Korea about his situation and has appealed the rejection of his asylum application in that country.
The activist fears he will end up in jail if deported to China
The activist said that he arrived in South Korea in late September with his wife, 8-year-old daughter and infant son.
Wang said he believed Chinese authorities were targeting him and that dozens of his staff members were arrested and questioned. Some remain in detention, he said. One staffer had his passport revoked while traveling from Thailand to Singapore last month, he said.
“The very same job has suddenly morphed from being praised into something associated with organized crime — it’s absolutely surreal,” said Wang.
Asked what he is afraid of if he is sent to China, Wang didn’t hesitate: “I would definitely spend the rest of my life behind bars.”
A notice reviewed by AP showed South Korean immigration authorities rejected Wang’s and his family’s applications for refugee status. AP also reviewed the U.S. Embassy email that revoked his visa, in which U.S. authorities told Wang that new information made him inadmissible to the U.S. or ineligible for a U.S. visa but did not provide specific details.
South Korea’s Justice Ministry said it couldn’t share any information, citing local laws on refugees and personal information protection.
Observers say that South Korea’s acceptance rate for refugee status applications has been less than 2% in recent years.
The U.S. State Department didn’t respond to the request for comment.
He was once praised as a ‘woodpecker’ rooting out fraud
Wang became a household name in China in the 1990s for exposing counterfeit goods, an increasingly widespread problem as the country’s market economy expanded rapidly and consumer protection oversight lagged.
In 1998, Wang joined a roundtable discussion with then-U.S. President Bill Clinton during his visit to Shanghai. Wang told Clinton he had been viewed as “immoral” at home, according to a White House transcript.
Chinese state media, however, largely portrayed him favorably, calling him “China’s No. 1 anti-counterfeiting activist.” Professional consumer advocates were compared to “woodpeckers,” rooting out problems in the marketplace.
Wang ran a rights-protection company in Beijing for about 30 years and a testing laboratory supporting anti-counterfeiting work for five years. He said both were forced to close after many of his staff, including three lawyers, were arrested in September.
The closure of his offices came after China launched its campaign against organized crime. Authorities said some people were using consumer complaints, lawsuits or threats of exposure to extort money from businesses through what officials called “malicious compensation claims.”
Some lawyers say consumer rights advocates play a positive role by exposing illegal practices, pressing businesses to address problems and helping authorities enforce regulations.
“The fact that some individuals engage in these activities as a profession or as a source of income does not invalidate the legitimacy of such social oversight itself,” said Zhang Yansheng, a Beijing-based lawyer.
After fleeing China, Wang seeks a new home with freedom
Wang’s consumer advocacy began more than three decades ago, when he suspected two pairs of Sony headphones he bought at a Beijing department store were counterfeit. He bought the remaining 10 pairs and secured compensation of twice the purchase price. It was widely celebrated on Chinese state media as a pioneering case of consumer activism.
He went on to run his own company and testing lab, helping consumers seek compensation and pushing for stronger consumer protections.
Wang and other advocates also pushed for a minimum compensation payment of 500 yuan ($75) for consumers, a proposal later incorporated into a revised consumer protection law in 2013.
His most recent case involved helping cherry farmers in the northeastern city of Dalian get compensation after they bought fake pesticide. He said Dalian police later arrested and detained around four dozen people including the cherry farmers, two lawyers who represented the farmers, and Wang’s staff.
Wang said he has since focused on researching asylum options and hopes to settle in the U.S., Canada, Britain, Australia or New Zealand, seeking what he called “real law enforcement and freedom” to “get away from China’s transnational repression.”
After his U.S. visa was revoked, Wang is seeking resettlement in Canada with the help of a human rights organization.
Fearing arrest by Chinese authorities even outside China, he said he and his family mostly stay indoors in South Korea. He said his bank accounts in China have been frozen, leaving the family in financial difficulty, and his 8-year-old daughter is struggling with her mental health because she cannot attend school.
AP writer Hyung-jin Kim in Seoul, South Korea, contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: J-20A at Airshow China 2026: First Display, Y-20B and Z-20T Debut
articles.title_zh: J-20A at Airshow China 2026: First Display, Y-20B and Z-20T Debut
articles.content_orig:
by Max Grünwald | Nov 27, 2026 | Aviation militaire , Nouvelles | 0 comments
China’s newest stealth fighter is finally coming out to play in public. On Thursday 26 November 2026, the People’s Liberation Army Air Force announced that the upgraded J-20A will make its first flying display at Airshow China in Zhuhai, while the re-engined Y-20B heavy transport goes on static display for the first time, with its cargo hold open to visitors.
A day later, on Friday 27 November, the PLA Army followed with its own line-up, headed by the debut of the Z-20T assault helicopter and the first indoor exhibition of the Type 100 tank. Together with the PLA Navy’s carrier aviation line-up announced on 23 November, which Afterburner covered here , the picture of China’s biggest military aviation shop window is now almost complete.
All details below come from Chinese state media: the PLA Air Force release as reported by China Daily, CCTV’s report carried by the Global Times and CCTV+, and the PLA Army’s WeChat release reported by the Global Times.
According to China Daily, the Air Force will send the J-20A and J-35A stealth fighters, the J-16 heavy multirole fighter, the Y-20B and the YY-20A aerial refuelling tanker to perform in the flying programme. In all, the Air Force says it will show more than 60 pieces of equipment across 33 types at the 16th China International Aviation and Aerospace Exhibition, which runs from 7 to 13 December.
Le J-20 itself is no stranger to Zhuhai: two of the stealth fighters made the type’s first public appearance with a flypast at Airshow China 2016. The J-20A is different. It was first shown in public at the Beijing military parade on 3 September 2025, and Zhuhai will be the first time it flies a display in front of an airshow crowd.
CCTV Video News Agency’s report on the PLA Air Force line-up for Airshow China 2026, published on 26 November 2026.
What has changed? Military affairs expert Song Zhongping told the Global Times that the J-20A brings improved avionics, flight-control and fire-control systems, and is powered by domestically developed engines with more thrust than those of earlier J-20s. Song said the stronger engines should improve acceleration and supersonic cruise. Beijing has not published official performance figures.
The Y-20 heavy transport made its public debut at Zhuhai back in 2014. The new star is the Y-20B, which will appear in the flying display and, for the first time, in the static park. Visitors will be able to walk into its cargo hold, according to the Air Force release reported by CCTV+.
Song told the Global Times that the main upgrade is the engine. Earlier Y-20s used Russian-made D-30KP-2 turbofans, while the Y-20B is fitted with the Chinese WS-20 high-bypass turbofan. In Song’s account, the original Y-20 design targeted a maximum payload of about 66 tonnes, which the older engines limited in practice, and the WS-20 should let the Y-20B come closer to that figure. The same airframe also underpins the YY-20A tanker, which will fly in the display, and the KJ-3000 airborne early warning aircraft.
On the ground the Air Force will also show a new-generation early-warning radar system for the first time. In the air, the August 1st aerobatic team will perform alongside two foreign teams: the Russian Knights of the Russian Aerospace Forces and the UAE Air Force ’s Al Fursan .
China Focus footage of the Y-20 at Airshow China 2024, two years before the Y-20B’s first static display.
The PLA Army announced on its WeChat account on Friday 27 November that it will have a dedicated indoor exhibition area at Airshow China for the first time. It will bring together 24 types of in-service frontline weapons across six categories, headed by the Type 100 tank, a new-generation tank that took part in the Beijing military parade on 3 September 2025.
In the air, the Army’s flying programme will feature the Z-10 attack helicopter, the Z-20 utility helicopter and the Z-20T, with the Z-20T making its Airshow China debut. The helicopters will carry assault troops and ground equipment in a coordinated demonstration simulating fire strikes and air assault operations, according to the Global Times report. All three types will also be on static display with rocket launchers and externally mounted seats.
Song Zhongping told the Global Times that the “T” stands for tuji , Chinese for “assault”, and that the Z-20T combines assault and transport roles in one airframe. The Z-20 has become the base platform for a whole family, including the naval Z-20J and Z-20F that the PLA Navy is bringing to the same show.
Airshow China 2026 coincides with the show’s 30th anniversary, according to CCTV+. With the Navy’s J-35 and KJ-600, the Air Force’s J-20A, J-35A and Y-20B and the Army’s Z-20T all on the programme, this edition looks set to put more new Chinese military hardware in front of the public than any before it.
Airshows are carefully staged, and a display routine reveals little about radar, engines or weapons. But for outside observers, Zhuhai is one of the very few chances to see these aircraft up close. Afterburner will be watching the skies over Zhuhai from 7 December.
Sources: Global Times, China Daily, CCTV+ (CCTV Video News Agency)

articles.title_zh: U.S. Proposes Section 301 Tariffs on 14 Economies; China Council for the Promotion of International Trade Urges Withdrawal
articles.content_orig:
Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged in Please refresh your browser to be logged in
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
China warned the US on Thursday that it “reserved the right” to retaliate against Donald Trump ’s latest tariffs, unveiled as the American president remained fixated on his divisive economic policy.
China was one of several Asian economies targeted on Wednesday with a fresh round of levies on certain imports, a major step towards bringing back some of the sweeping global tariffs Mr Trump imposed last year, only to see the US Supreme Court strike them down in February.
China and Vietnam were hit with the steepest proposed tariffs, while Japan, South Korea, Indonesia, India, Malaysia, Singapore, Taiwan, Thailand, Bangladesh, and Cambodia also faced significant levies. The EU and Switzerland were targeted as well.
China, one of the largest trading partners of the US, faces 20 per cent tariffs over allegations of manufacturing overcapacity. The allegation is that the Asian economic giant is making far more industrial stuff than domestic and global demand can absorb. The levies could rise to as much as 40 per cent for China and 35 percent for Vietnam if Washington determines they aren’t complying with existing trade agreements.
“China urges the US to correct its wrong practices and return to the right track of resolving issues through dialogue and consultation,” commerce ministry spokesperson He Yadong said, adding that Beijing “reserves the right to take necessary measures and will resolutely safeguard its legitimate rights and interests”.
He urged the US to accelerate internal procedures to put a $60 billion tariff reduction arrangement into effect as soon as possible, adding that American and Chinese officials had kept communication over their trade truce.
A Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson accused the US of using claims of industrial overcapacity as a pretext for “political manipulation”.
“The so-called overcapacity is a false proposition and China opposes using it as a pretext for political manipulation,” he said.
“China and the US should work together to implement the important consensus reached between the two heads of state and maintain the momentum of stable development in bilateral economic and trade relations.”
The tariffs were proposed following an investigation led by Mr Trump’s trade negotiator Jamieson Greer into whether foreign trade practices violated existing agreements, or discriminated against American goods.
The fresh round of levies came after the Supreme Court ruled the president’s “Liberation Day” tariffs unlawful in February. The new duties are meant to match the rates agreed upon in trade deals struck since Mr Trump unleashed his trade war.
Under a trade agreement reached earlier this year, China was subject to a 10 per cent reciprocal tariff, in addition to a 10 per cent levy linked to fentanyl. The newly proposed tariff rate of 20 per cent could double if US officials determine that Beijing has failed to honour the terms of the earlier trade truce.
The latest tariff announcement threatened to strain relations between Washington and Beijing barely days after Mr Trump and Chinese president Xi Jinping held talks on the sidelines of the Apec summit in Shenzhen. The two leaders are expected to meet again in Miami next month.
The fragile trade truce between Washington and Beijing is set to expire on 10 January. It limits new US tariff increases to 20 percentage points on top of existing levies of 25 percent going back to Mr Trump’s first term. The latest proposal reaches that ceiling.
Under the latest tariff measures, Japan, Taiwan and South Korea face rates of 15 percent.
India faces a tariff of 25 percent, which may be lowered to 17 percent if a trade deal is done. Thailand, Bangladesh, and Cambodia face proposed rates of up to 18 percent. Indonesia and Malaysia are seeking to retain previously agreed rates of 19 percent. Vietnam remains in talks with Washington for a trade deal.

articles.title_orig: Tech German software major SAP is reportedly weighing cutting at least 10,000 jobs in AI push
articles.title_zh: Tech German software major SAP is reportedly weighing cutting at least 10,000 jobs in AI push
articles.content_orig:
SAP is preparing a plan to eliminate at least 10,000 positions as the German firm reshapes its software business for the artificial intelligence era, Bloomberg reported on Thursday , citing people familiar with the matter.
The report came as the company flagged a cybersecurity attack, but said it had found "no evidence of unauthorized access to customer business data."
"SAP has identified suspicious activity and promptly implemented the necessary measures to protect its customers and preserve the security of its services," a company spokesperson said.
"Our customers trust us to protect their data, and that remains our highest priority. In a highly dynamic threat environment, we will continue to strengthen our security to provide the secure and resilient environment our customers depend on."
The company did not respond to a request for comment on the reported job cuts. The number could change after labor negotiations.
Other software companies have also tied workforce reductions to AI initiatives, though for different reasons. WiseTech Global said in February it planned to cut about 2,000 jobs over two years as it integrated AI into its products and operations.
Atlassian said in March it would cut about 1,600 jobs partly to fund further AI investment, while Cloudflare said in May it would eliminate more than 1,100 roles as it moved toward an AI-first operating model.
In the U.S., employers cited AI in 121,401 job-cut announcements through October 2026, accounting for about 20% of the total, according to a Nov. 5 report from outplacement and executive coaching firm Challenger, Gray & Christmas.
SAP employs more than 110,000 people worldwide. Bloomberg reported that all departments had been asked to identify potential cuts, with product, engineering and sales in particular focus.
The company also underwent a reorganization in 2024, when it eliminated around 10,000 positions through a program that relied mainly on voluntary departures and retraining.
Its headcount later remained relatively flat as it hired for new roles, Bloomberg reported.
In 2023, SAP CEO Christian Klein told CNBC he did not necessarily expect a reduction in the workforce, saying he expected the company to grow and "accelerate" its total revenue.
The reported cuts come as Klein pushes SAP toward an AI-first strategy . This year, SAP completed four acquisitions — Reltio, Dremio, Prior Labs and TechWolf — and made strategic investments in AI-focused companies including Parloa, n8n and Conduct.
The acquisitions are intended to help SAP organize company data, develop AI models for business information and analyze workforce skills.

articles.title_orig: McKinsey: China's scale hard to match
articles.title_zh: McKinsey: China's scale hard to match
articles.content_orig:
Multinational companies can work with Chinese partners to develop products in China and bring them to global markets, drawing on a combination of scale, deep supply chains and rapid innovation that is difficult to replicate elsewhere, McKinsey's Greater China chairman said.
Joe Ngai made the remarks in Shanghai at the launch of the Chinese edition of The Next China Is Still China on Nov 25, having co-authored the book with Nick Leung, a former chairman of the firm's Greater China office.
Ngai cited Volkswagen's partnership with Chinese electric vehicle maker Xpeng as an example of how multinationals can tap local expertise. He also noted growing scope for Chinese companies to bring their technologies and intellectual property to overseas markets. Looking ahead, areas to watch include the use of artificial intelligence in manufacturing, the expansion of Chinese robotics companies overseas and licensing deals for innovative drugs.
"The competition in AI is now about how companies use it," Ngai said, adding that companies' ability to reorganize teams and change how they work will help determine whether they can deploy AI at scale.
A 2025 McKinsey survey showed that 84 percent of respondents in China felt positive about AI products and services, compared with 69 percent in South Korea, 67 percent in Singapore, 46 percent in Japan, 45 percent in Germany, 38 percent in the United States and 31 percent in Canada.
China has more than 5,000 AI companies and has released more than 1,500 large language models, according to figures presented at the event.
Ngai and Leung highlighted that narrower margins and tougher competition are making growth harder to achieve. They see new opportunities in technological innovation and closer integration with global markets, as companies build the capacity to shape markets at home and abroad.

articles.title_orig: Regional relations, modern munitions will poise U.S. to defeat China, Trump pick to lead Navy says
articles.title_zh: Regional relations, modern munitions will poise U.S. to defeat China, Trump pick to lead Navy says
articles.content_orig:
U.S. President Donald Trump delivers remarks on reciprocal tariffs during an event at the White House on April 2, 2025.
China warned Thursday that it reserves the right to take “necessary measures” to retaliate against the Trump Administration’s proposed new tariffs , which have reignited global trade tensions.
“China urges the U.S. to correct its wrong practices and return to the right track of resolving issues through dialogue and consultation,” said He Yadong, spokesperson for the Ministry of Commerce. He added that Beijing “reserves the right to take necessary measures and will resolutely safeguard its legitimate rights and interests.”
The Trump Administration targeted 14 trading partners Wednesday in a slew of new tariffs that are set to come into effect early next year. The levies will be imposed under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 following an investigation led by U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer. The U.S. said the probe had found demonstrations of unfair trade practices and excess manufacturing capacity. Mexico and Norway were not listed in the new proposals, as investigations into their respective trade practices are ongoing. Greer framed the tariffs as a way to “level the playing field for American workers and chart a new, more sustainable course for the world economy.” The Section 301 avenue is a way for the Trump Administration to reinstate many of the tariffs that were deemed illegal and struck down by the Supreme Court in February.
China is facing a 20% tariff, which the Trump Administration said it could double to 40% if Beijing does not adhere to the terms of an existing trade truce with Washington.
Another major U.S. trading partner, Vietnam, is facing tariffs of up to 35%. The country’s Ministry of Industry and Trade said it was in the process of “developing and submitting counter-arguments to the preliminary conclusions and inaccurate opinions and allegations from relevant parties.”
Agathe Demarais, a senior policy fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations, views the tariff proposals as a pressure point on Southeast Asian economies and their trade relations with the U.S. and China.
She says that many of the region’s economies see a lot of Chinese goods pass through before heading to the U.S. market, with tariffs intended to “make it more difficult for economies like Vietnam to position themselves as collector economies between the U.S. and China,” she tells TIME.
The proposed tariffs are subject to a public notice and comment period, with a hearing set to take place early next year before they go into effect, allowing countries to issue responses and arguments.
Deborah Elms, head of trade policy at the Singapore-based Hinrich Foundation, says the proposed measures are already generating significant “resentment” among trading partners.
On top of that, the proposed rates have prompted uncertainty for major economies as to what Washington could do next. “If the U.S. unilaterally determines that the partner is not living up to expectations, then the number can ramp up higher,” she says. “That doesn't really support trust, and it makes it very hard to plan ahead.”
Amid rising tensions, several trading partners are already following China’s lead in voicing their disapproval over the rates.
Bernd Lange, trade committee chair in the European Parliament, said it was “absurd” the E.U. is facing a 20% tariff. He expressed hope that any enforced tariffs will adhere to the Turnberry agreement signed between Washington and the E.U. last year, which capped U.S. tariffs at 15%.
“Washington’s allegations about E.U. industrial overcapacity are absurd. We’ll now see whether the announced U.S. tariffs comply with Turnberry in practice,” he said. “If Washington breaches its commitments, the E.U. must act swiftly. It has the legal means to do so.”
Elms says the threat to hike rates against economies that already have a trade pact with the U.S. further calls into question “how durable” trade commitments with Washington are.
Overall, the proposed rates are just “one more complication in the relationship with the U.S.” that global partners have to contend with, adds Demarais.
Singapore and Japan also hit back at the prospect of respective 20% tariff rates.
Singapore’s Ministry of Energy, Trade, and Industry said it was “very disappointed” by the assessment and argued that the U.S. Trade Representative’s findings “do not take into account the structure of Singapore’s economy.” Japan’s Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara referred to the U.S. tariffs as “regrettable,” insisting that: “Japan does not have any nonmarket policies or practices, or structural excess production capacity in the first place.”
Alongside the sweeping tariffs against 14 trading partners, the Trump Administration published a separate proposal seeking to raise levies on Brazil by specifically targeting its sugar and aircraft exports.
“Imposing an additional, specific tariff on sugar imports from Brazil and an additional 10% tariff on finished aircraft exports from Brazil is intended to help bring Brazil to the table,” said the office of the USTR (U.S. Trade Representative). The announcement came amid stalled trade talks between Washington and Brazil.
The Brazilian government expressed “outrage” over the proposed raising of rates, arguing that it has “been acting in good faith in negotiations” relating to Section 301 with the U.S. for over a year.
“The USTR's unilateral decision constitutes an unacceptable action within the ongoing bilateral negotiation process. Brazil will not yield to this type of threat,” the government vowed in a statement.
It said Brazil would continue to negotiate with the U.S., “without ruling out the possibility of adopting retaliatory measures in response to the illegal and unjust imposition of tariffs on Brazilian products.”
The Trump Administration could face significant pushback from the U.S. Congress next year, as Democrats will take control of both the House and Senate in January following sweeping victories in the midterms.
Senator Ron Wyden of Oregon, who will chair the Senate Finance Committee next year, has vowed to try and overturn Trump’s tariffs.
“This is another blatant attempt by Donald Trump to reconstruct his illegal global tariffs, no matter the cost to American families, workers, and small businesses. Global overcapacity is a serious problem, but Trump’s unilateral price-hiking tariffs are not the solution,” Wyden said in a statement . “As incoming Finance Committee Chairman, I will use every tool at my disposal to end Trump’s tariff chaos and restore Congress’ constitutional authority over trade.”
However, securing a veto-proof majority to rein in Trump’s authority could well prove difficult.
Among the general public, tariffs remain deeply unpopular with Americans. An NBC News exit poll following the midterm elections found that 66% of voters believed Trump’s tariff policies had hurt the national economy.

articles.content_orig:
